fund_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare Y Combinator SAFE documents for our pre-seed raise using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops document automation tool. This step requires my explicit approval before anything is sent or finalized, so you must prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: our company legal name and state of incorporation, the SAFE type we're using (post-money, valuation cap and/or discount, or MFN), the target raise amount, a list of prospective investors (name, email, intended investment amount), and confirmation of {{vendor}} account access via my configured credentials.

Then, using {{vendor}}:
1. Complete the guided questionnaire for each SAFE, entering our company details, chosen SAFE terms, and each investor's information.
2. Let {{vendor}} auto-populate the standard YC SAFE template with these answers rather than drafting from scratch.
3. Note any fields or choices {{vendor}} flags as needing attorney review, and compile these into a clear list with the specific clause and why it was flagged.
4. Generate a draft (unsigned) SAFE document for each investor and save/export them in one place I can review.
5. Prepare a summary checklist showing: investor name, amount, SAFE terms used, document status (draft ready), and any flagged review items.

Do not send any document for signature, submit anything to investors, or mark any document as final — only prepare drafts and the review checklist, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the list of generated draft SAFEs (investor, amount, terms), the compiled attorney-review flags, and confirmation that all documents are staged in {{vendor}} awaiting my approval before distribution.

fund_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up an investor pipeline tracker for our pre-seed SAFE fundraise using {{vendor}}, our project-management tool. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/team details, (2) the list of target investor names, firms, and any known contact info I want pre-loaded, and (3) the pipeline stages I want to track (e.g., Sourced, Contacted, Meeting Scheduled, Pitched, Due Diligence, Committed, Passed, Closed).

Using your configured credentials, do the following via {{vendor}}'s API:
1. Create a pipeline tracker structure (a list or database) dedicated to this fundraise.
2. Customize fields to match our process: investor name, firm, contact, check size/target, stage/status, last contact date, next follow-up date, and notes.
3. For each investor I provide, create a task (using the create-task API) capturing their details, current stage, and — where relevant — a due date for the next follow-up action, assigned to me.
4. Create at least one view (using the create-view API) to organize and visualize the pipeline by stage, and if supported, set up a board view for stage-based tracking and a list or timeline view for follow-up dates.
5. Confirm the tracker supports multiple view types (board, list, calendar/timeline) so we can review pipeline health different ways.

When done, report back: the tracker/database name and location in {{vendor}}, the field/stage schema you configured, the number of investor tasks created (with a sample of 2-3), the views created, and any investors from my list you couldn't add (with reasons). Flag any API limitations you hit so I can adjust manually if needed.

fund_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me draft investor outreach emails for my pre-seed SAFE fundraise using {{vendor}}, my connected email tool. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (1) my startup's one-paragraph pitch/description, (2) the target raise amount and SAFE terms (valuation cap, discount if any), (3) a list of target investors (name, email, firm, and any personalization notes like mutual connections or prior interest), and (4) any founder background points I want highlighted (traction, team, prior exits, etc.).

Once you have this, draft a personalized outreach email for each investor using {{vendor}}'s draft creation capability. Each draft should: be concise (under 200 words), written in a warm but professional founder voice, reference something specific to that investor (their portfolio, thesis, or connection), briefly state what we're building and traction, mention we're raising a pre-seed round on a YC SAFE with the terms I gave you, and end with a clear, low-friction ask (e.g., a 15-minute call). If I have any saved templates or snippets for outreach, use those as a base and fill in variables per investor rather than writing generic boilerplate each time.

Save all drafts in {{vendor}} — do not send anything. Once drafts are created, give me a summary list: investor name, subject line, and a one-line description of the personalization angle used for each, so I can quickly review.

Because sending requires my explicit approval, do not send any emails. Prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off so I can review and approve each draft before it goes out.

fund_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me manage logistics around investor meetings for my pre-seed SAFE fundraise. The actual meetings (relationship-building, pitching, and real-time negotiation) are conversations I must conduct myself — this remains a human step you cannot perform. Your job is to prepare and track everything around those meetings.

First, ask me for anything you need: my target investor list (names, firms, emails), my pitch deck link or file, my data room link, my calendar availability, and any CRM or spreadsheet I already use to track outreach (e.g., Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion).

Then do the following:
1. Build or update a tracker (spreadsheet or doc) listing each investor with columns for: contact info, meeting status (not scheduled / scheduled / completed / follow-up sent), meeting date, notes, and next action.
2. Draft personalized meeting confirmation emails and follow-up/thank-you emails for each investor, referencing their firm and any prior context I give you, ready for me to review and send.
3. Prepare a pre-meeting briefing note for each scheduled meeting summarizing the investor's background, focus areas, and suggested talking points based on public information I provide or that you can find.
4. Set up reminders or a checklist for me to poll: after each meeting date passes, prompt me to log the outcome and any next steps (e.g., send SAFE terms, schedule follow-up, decline).

Done looks like: a complete, up-to-date investor meeting tracker, drafted emails ready for my review, briefing notes for upcoming meetings, and a polling checklist so I remember to update statuses after each meeting occurs.

Report back with: the tracker link/location, a summary of drafted emails awaiting my send approval, and a list of meetings still needing status updates from me. Do not attempt to conduct, join, or simulate the investor conversations themselves — only prepare materials and track status.

fund_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me send YC Standard SAFE documents for e-signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform, as part of closing our pre-seed round. Use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}}.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) the finalized SAFE document(s) or the specific YC SAFE variant and terms (valuation cap, discount, MFN) already agreed per investor, (2) the list of investors with legal name, entity name (if applicable), and signer email addresses, (3) our company signer's name, title, and email, and (4) the correct signing order/routing (e.g., investor signs first, then founder countersigns, or vice versa).

Then, for each investor: populate a SAFE document with the investor's name, entity, investment amount, and agreed terms; create a signature envelope/request in {{vendor}} with the correct recipients and routing order; attach the populated SAFE; and set field tags/signature blocks for both the investor and our company signer. Prepare one envelope per investor (or a batch if the platform supports it), and double-check that names, amounts, and terms match our records exactly before finalizing.

Do not click send. Once all envelopes are fully prepared and populated, compile a summary for me listing each investor, the amount, terms, and envelope status (drafted/ready to send), plus a checklist confirming documents and recipients are correct. Then stop for human sign-off — I will personally review and approve sending each envelope. Report back with this summary and flag any investor whose terms or contact details are missing or ambiguous so I can resolve them before signature requests go out.

fund_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me verify that pre-seed SAFE investor wire transfers have been received in our company bank account via {{vendor}}. Use our {{vendor}} account (accessed through our configured credentials).

First, ask me for: (1) the list of investors who committed to wiring funds, with expected amounts and expected timeframe for each, and (2) confirmation of which checking account should be receiving these wires if we have more than one.

Then do the following:
1. Retrieve our business checking account(s) to confirm which account is set up to receive the SAFE wires.
2. Pull recent balance history on that account to spot incoming deposits matching the expected wire amounts and dates.
3. List recent banking transactions on the account to identify and confirm each incoming wire, matching sender name/reference and amount against the investor list I gave you.
4. Cross-reference every expected investor against the transactions found, and produce a clear reconciliation table with columns: Investor, Expected Amount, Wire Received (Y/N), Actual Amount, Date Received, Notes (e.g., partial payment, mismatched amount, sender name discrepancy).
5. Flag any expected wires not yet received, and any received wires that don't match an expected investor or amount.
6. If {{vendor}} supports webhook subscriptions for new transactions, note whether one is already configured for ongoing monitoring, but do not set up new automations beyond checking existing configuration.

Done looks like: a complete reconciliation table covering all expected investors, with discrepancies and missing wires clearly flagged, based on actual transaction data pulled from {{vendor}}.

Report back to me with: the reconciliation table, a summary count of wires received vs. outstanding, and a list of any anomalies needing my attention. Do not take any action on the funds (no transfers, categorizations, or approvals) — just verify and report.

fund_001:n8.prompt:
You are helping me update our capitalization table in {{vendor}} to record a newly closed SAFE note as part of our pre-seed fundraise.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if you don't already have them: the investor's legal name and contact details, the SAFE's purchase amount, valuation cap, discount rate, the execution date, and the {{vendor}} issuer/company identifier if applicable. Use my configured credentials to connect to {{vendor}}.

Actions to take:
1. Pull our current cap table and full stakeholder list from {{vendor}} to establish the pre-transaction baseline.
2. Prepare a draft entry for the new SAFE — investor name, amount, cap, discount, and date — modeled with its conversion terms as {{vendor}} supports.
3. Reconcile the draft against our existing data room records to confirm no duplicate or conflicting entries exist.
4. Pull the cap table and stakeholder list again in preview/staged form (if {{vendor}} supports a preview or draft state) so I can see exactly what will change before anything is committed.
5. Compile a summary showing: prior ownership by share class, the new SAFE entry, and resulting post-transaction ownership/dilution.

Do not submit, finalize, or apply the update in {{vendor}} yourself — a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied. Prepare everything (the draft SAFE entry, reconciliation notes, and before/after cap table summary) and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the baseline cap table snapshot, the prepared SAFE entry details, any discrepancies found during reconciliation, and the projected post-transaction cap table, clearly flagged as pending my approval before being applied in {{vendor}}.

fund_001:n9.prompt: You are helping me prepare (but NOT submit) our SEC Form D filing for our pre-seed SAFE round, required within 15 days of the first sale of securities. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our legal entity name, EIN, state/jurisdiction and date of incorporation, (2) principal office address, (3) names/addresses of executive officers, directors, and any promoters, (4) the date of first sale in this offering, (5) total offering amount and amount sold to date, (6) number of investors and whether any are non-accredited, (7) the exemption being claimed (Rule 506(b) or 506(c)), (8) our EDGAR/SEC filer credentials status (use your configured credentials if you have programmatic access; otherwise note that a human will log in manually), and (9) the name and title of the authorized signer who will certify the filing. Using this information, draft a complete Form D data set formatted exactly as required by the SEC's EDGAR online filing system at https://www.onlineforms.edgarfiling.sec.gov/, including all issuer information, offering details, and related persons. Organize this into a clear checklist/summary document so the authorized signer can review every field before submission. Do not log in, enter data into EDGAR, certify, sign, or submit the filing yourself — filing Form D requires an authorized company representative to legally attest to the disclosures, so you must stop for human sign-off once the draft and checklist are ready. Report back with: the completed draft Form D field-by-field summary, any missing or ambiguous information you need from me, and a short list of final verification steps for the human filer to complete before they submit.

fund_001:n10.prompt:
You are helping me send the closing confirmation email for my YC SAFE pre-seed round to all participating investors, using {{vendor}} as the email tool. Before drafting, ask me for anything you need that's missing: the list of investor names and email addresses, the round details (SAFE type, valuation cap/discount, total amount raised, closing date), a link or reference to the signed SAFE documents, and the sender inbox/account you should use with {{vendor}}.

Once you have this, draft a clear, professional closing confirmation email that: thanks the investor, confirms their specific investment amount and SAFE terms, states the official closing date, references where signed documents and wire instructions live (or confirms funds received if applicable), and gives a point of contact for questions. Personalize each draft per investor rather than sending one generic blast.

Prepare these drafts as individual messages ready to send via {{vendor}}'s documented API or connected inbox access (e.g., composing and queuing send-message calls), but do NOT actually send anything yet. Show me the full list of recipients with their personalized draft text, the sender address, and a summary of round details being confirmed, so I can review for accuracy before anything goes out. Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the drafts — do not send, submit, or dispatch any email yourself.

When done, report back with: the number of investor drafts prepared, the {{vendor}} inbox/account used, a copy of each draft for my review, and a note confirming everything is staged and awaiting my explicit approval to send.
